requirement: Coil NTC 120C shutdown, 100C recovery (docs/STRATEGY.md; docs/FUNCTIONAL_TEST_CRITERIA.md SS2.3)
reason: Exactly one `ThermalComparator` module is defined in elec/src/modules.ato, and it is instantiated exactly once: `thermal = new ThermalComparator` inside SafetyInterlock (elec/src/modules.ato ~line 1790). There is no second instance, and no second NTC-divider+comparator chain of any kind in elec/src/modules.ato or elec/src/main.ato.

The one instantiated ThermalComparator's NTC (mpn NTCALUG01A104GA) is documented by its own inline comment as 'lug-mount on heatsink' -- consistent with THM-01 (heatsink), not THM-02 (coil). No coil-mounted NTC circuit exists to be THM-02's implementation.

docs/hardware/BOM.md's NTC-related line items are NTC_INRUSH (the AC inrush limiter thermistor, unrelated to over-temperature protection) and a single NTC_IGBT (Murata NCU18XH103F6SRB, 10kohm/B=3950 @ 25C) -- note this BOM part NUMBER AND VALUE differs from the part actually wired into ThermalComparator in elec/src/modules.ato (Vishay NTCALUG01A104GA, 100kohm/B=4190 @ 25C). That is a second, independent BOM-vs-schematic source contradiction (component identity, not just value) worth flagging alongside the OCP-02 finding. Neither BOM entry is a coil sensor.

docs/plans/2026-07-24-002-feat-pivot-to-fab-ready-board-verdict-plan.md independently confirms this gap from the firmware side: 'THM is a single generic EVENT_OVER_TEMP with no heatsink-vs-coil distinction' -- the firmware state machine has no separate coil-thermal event either, consistent with there being no coil hardware to generate one.
